clue.text: Novel written in an attic?

parts.note: surface reading: a book whose author worked up in the loft
setter's reading: the title of John Braine's 1957 novel describes exactly where an attic room is

explanation.walkthrough: John Braine's novel about social climbing in postwar Yorkshire is called Room at the Top; an attic is literally such a room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the title of a famous English novel, and an attic is the highest room in a house.

clue.text: Algeria's abandoned trappings of state

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters are let loose into a new order

parts.note: the country's name taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A North African country has given up its ceremonial pomp.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty or office, such as crown and sceptre, carried on state occasions.

clue.text: This protection's best of the lot!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a loose protective coat or garment worn over clothes
second meaning: as in the winner across every category of a competition

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the two senses: a protective garment, and the adjective for a champion across all events.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall is a workwear smock; an overall winner is top when all results are combined.

clue.text: Hearings in case due to be rescheduled

indicators.note: rescheduling rearranges things, so these letters will be put in a different order

explanation.surface: Court hearings for a case that is coming up are being moved to new dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearings' suggests the courtroom, but here it means formal interviews.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal meeting with a dignitary, a chance to be heard, so hearings is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Why bridegroom will go to church, dragged along

definitions.text: Why bridegroom will go to church
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: his purpose there is marriage
second meaning: pulled behind a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: Split as TO WED it answers the question of the groom's errand; as one word it means pulled by a tow rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A car hauled behind a truck by a rope has been towed, i.e. dragged along behind.

clue.text: Unreliable quote about a bishop getting up

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from bottom to top
about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the others

parts.note: Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A misquote attributed to a bishop who is rising to speak cannot be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend is the formal style of a bishop, hence the doubled R; the whole container is turned upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic behaves irregularly and unpredictably, so it cannot be depended upon.

clue.text: Hero and son at sea but not at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hero and his son are out on the ocean, yet somehow also on dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase does both jobs: first 'at sea' as confused, then 'not at sea' literally as on land.
explanation.definitionFit: Onshore means on the land rather than out on the water, the opposite of being afloat.

clue.text: Typically Lincoln's for living in, under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something places it lower, after the other piece

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
a residential building is one meant to be lived in

explanation.surface: Lincoln's house was built to live in while under great stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham Lincoln was a US president, so something typical of him is presidential.
explanation.definitionFit: As a US head of state, Lincoln's manner and office were characteristic of a president.

clue.text: We raged about plant inducing hay fever

indicators.note: about can mean scattered around, so these letters are tossed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Hay fever sufferers fume about the weed that set off their sneezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a weed whose abundant pollen is a leading cause of allergic rhinitis in North America.

clue.text: Feels more animated with guns mounted

parts.note: W is a common abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone livens up once the artillery is in position.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm up is to become livelier or more enthusiastic, as a crowd does as an event goes on.

clue.text: Reserve allocated to specific team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set aside for later
second meaning, read literally: placed on one of the two sides

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for keeping something back, and literally describes picking a player for one particular side.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on one side is to save or set apart for later, just as a reserve is kept back.

clue.text: Recovered goods left during attack

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to savage is to attack fiercely
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Stolen property was abandoned in the middle of an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is property rescued from a wreck, fire or disaster, i.e. goods that have been retrieved.

clue.text: Tried to supply US industrial centre

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a bendy flexible way, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: An attempt was made to provide goods to an American manufacturing hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb to provide, but it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit, Michigan, is the historic home of the American car-making business.

clue.text: Type of delivery to take out learner

parts.note: to draw a sword or money is to take it out
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A cricket ball is bowled in a way meant to dismiss a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' suggests a bowled ball, but it is a way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened manner of speaking, so it describes how words are delivered.

clue.text: Reveal all and sing — it's what we should do in the shower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to confess everything, as an informer sings to the police

definitions.text: what we should do in the shower
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: emerge washed

explanation.walkthrough: Singing in the shower is the picture, but sing is slang for confess; the idiom also literally describes coming out washed.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is to own up completely, telling the whole truth one had been hiding.

clue.text: Losing track of motorway carnage

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as MI

explanation.surface: A dreadful pile-up on the motorway makes us lose our way.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read its digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mislaying something is to put it somewhere and forget where, thereby losing it.

clue.text: Botanists short of a pound? They needn't spend much on clothes

definitions.text: They needn't spend much on clothes

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: A plus L, the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Plant scientists low on money will at least save on their wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A and L out of NATURALISTS to leave NATURISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists are nudists, who go without garments and so have little need to buy any.

clue.text: A small company added to bill for sauce

indicators.note: adding one thing to another places it after, joining the pieces end to end

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar
S is the abbreviation for small
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A little firm puts a surcharge on the bill for a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a brand of hot pepper condiment from Louisiana.

clue.text: Try to slash regular charge for clothing

indicators.note: slashing cuts into something, so one piece is thrust inside the other

parts.note: to aim to do something is to try

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to cut the monthly fee charged for their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for garments, attire worn on the body.

clue.text: Let out new clothing DI brought back

indicators.note: bringing back means returning, so the letters are read right to left
clothing something covers it, so one word is wrapped around the other

explanation.surface: A detective inspector has been released and given fresh clothes on his return.
explanation.walkthrough: DI stands for Detective Inspector, a British police rank; 'Let out' is the dressmaker's sense, not release.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting out a garment makes it wider, enlarging its seams to broaden it.

clue.text: Bear up amid very little cheer

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside another
in a down entry, up means the letters run from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A small teddy bear is held up while folk cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear is Winnie-the-Pooh, A. A. Milne's honey-loving toy; wee is Scottish for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoopee is an exclamation of delight, a cry of joy or celebration.

clue.text: Aimless productions? Director has a great many

indicators.note: having something means it comes along next, so the pieces are joined

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: A film director churns out plenty of pointless projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Productions' and 'Director' suggest film, but the definition is cryptic: pointless scribbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodles are idle drawings made without purpose, so they are productions with no aim.

clue.text: How barrister's given instruction to sum up

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: a barrister is instructed by means of a written case summary from a solicitor
second meaning: briefly, as a concluding summary

explanation.walkthrough: A barrister is a courtroom lawyer in Britain; solicitors instruct one by sending a brief, a document outlining the case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in summary, used before a short concluding restatement.

clue.text: Deadly soubriquet for portly gangster?

explanation.surface: A deadly nickname given to an overweight mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat Al would be a nickname for a stout Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal means causing death, the same as lethal or deadly.

clue.text: A room arranged by American in love

indicators.note: something arranged has been set in order, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: An American has prepared a room for romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means feeling or showing romantic desire, the state of being smitten.

clue.text: The woman possessed by passion's most lavish

indicators.note: something possessed is held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman gripped by desire is at her most extravagant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush means luxuriant or rich, so the superlative is the most opulent.

clue.text: Rascal troubled, we hear, getting stuck

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: ailed means troubled, as in what ailed him

explanation.surface: A naughty child was upset, apparently, and got stuck somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: impaled means having been stuck through, which 'getting stuck' paraphrases.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impaled is to be pierced through by a spike, getting stuck on it.

clue.text: Pays for fellers, those on the march

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Someone covers the cost for the lads, the ones on the protest march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellers' looks like informal 'fellows' but means tree-cutters.
explanation.definitionFit: Footsloggers are infantry soldiers or walkers who trudge long distances on foot.
